name.text: Finding the mistake in a bisector construction

questiontext.text:
{@nm[1]@} constructed the perpendicular bisector of a line segment \(AB\) of length \({@L@}\) cm. {@nm[2]@} wrote:

  1. Draw \(AB = {@L@}\) cm.

  2. Open the compasses to {@exd(R1)@} cm.

  3. With the point at \(A\), draw an arc above \(AB\) and an arc below \(AB\).

  4. [[if test="is(er=2)"]]Open the compasses to {@exd(R2)@} cm, put the point at \(B\) and draw an arc above \(AB\) and an arc below \(AB\).[[else]]Without changing the compasses, put the point at \(B\) and draw an arc above \(AB\) and an arc below \(AB\).[[/if]]

  5. [[if test="is(er=3)"]]Join the point where the arcs cross above \(AB\) to \(B\).[[else]]Join the two points where the arcs cross.[[/if]]

The diagram shows the construction drawn exactly as written.

[[jsxgraph width="340px" height="220px"]] (function () { var L = {#L#}, R1 = {#float(R1)#}, R2 = {#float(RB)#}, er = {#er#}; var x = (L * L + R1 * R1 - R2 * R2) / (2 * L), h2 = R1 * R1 - x * x, y, tA, tB; if (h2 > 0) { y = Math.sqrt(h2); tA = Math.atan2(y, x); tB = Math.atan2(y, x - L); } else { y = 0; tA = 1.1; tB = Math.PI - 1.1; } // The height grows with the crossing points so the arcs are never cut off at the top or bottom var top = Math.max(5.2, y + 1.6); var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-1.6, top, L + 1.6, -top], keepAspectRatio: true, axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); var A = b.create('point', [0, 0], {name: 'A', fixed: true, size: 2, color: '#000000', label: {offset: [-14, -10]}}); var B = b.create('point', [L, 0], {name: 'B', fixed: true, size: 2, color: '#000000', label: {offset: [6, -10]}}); b.create('segment', [A, B], {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); function arc(cx, R, t) { b.create('curve', [function (s) { return cx + R * Math.cos(s); }, function (s) { return R * Math.sin(s); }, t - 0.4, t + 0.4], {strokeColor: '#1f4e9c', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } arc(0, R1, tA); arc(0, R1, -tA); arc(L, R2, tB); arc(L, R2, -tB); if (er === 2) { b.create('line', [[x, y], [x, -y]], {strokeColor: '#b00000', strokeWidth: 1.5, straightFirst: false, straightLast: false, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } if (er === 3) { b.create('segment', [[x, y], B], {strokeColor: '#b00000', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) What does the mistake do?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The correct construction is:

  1. Draw \(AB = {@L@}\) cm.

  2. Open the compasses to more than half of \(AB\), that is more than {@exd(L/2)@} cm.

  3. With the point at \(A\), draw an arc above \(AB\) and an arc below \(AB\).

  4. Without changing the compasses, put the point at \(B\) and draw an arc above and an arc below \(AB\).

  5. Join the two points where the arcs cross.

Each crossing point is one radius from \(A\) and the same radius from \(B\), so it is equidistant from \(A\) and \(B\). That is why the radius must be more than half of \(AB\) (or the arcs do not meet) and must stay the same for both ends.

[[if test="is(er=1)"]]The mistake is in Step 2: {@exd(R1)@} cm is less than half of \(AB\), so the arcs from \(A\) and \(B\) do not meet.[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]The mistake is in Step 4: the compasses were changed to {@exd(R2)@} cm, so the crossing points are not equidistant from \(A\) and \(B\). The line joining them is still at right angles to \(AB\), but it does not pass through the midpoint.[[else]]The mistake is in Step 5: the line must join the two crossing points. Joining one crossing point to \(B\) gives a line that does not cross \(AB\) at right angles.[[/if]]

node.description: Blamed a step that is right once the others are

truefeedback.text: [[if test="is(er=3)"]]The radius in Step 2, {@exd(R1)@} cm, is more than half of \(AB\) and is kept for Step 4, so the arcs are right. Look at which points are joined.[[else]]Step 5 is right once the arcs are right: the line through the two crossing points is the perpendicular bisector. The mistake is earlier.[[/if]]

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(er=1)"]]Step 4 keeps the compasses as they were, which is what the construction needs. Look at the diagram: do the arcs from \(A\) and from \(B\) meet? Which step decides that?[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]The radius in Step 2, {@exd(R1)@} cm, is more than half of \(AB\) ({@exd(L/2)@} cm), so the arcs from \(A\) are right. Follow the compasses through the later steps.[[else]]Step 4 keeps the compasses as they were, so the arcs are right and they cross above and below \(AB\). Look at what is done with the crossing points.[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: There is a mistake in the working; find it in part (a).

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(er=1)"]]No line is drawn in the diagram, so nothing crosses \(AB\). Look at the arcs: each has radius {@exd(R1)@} cm, and \(AB = {@L@}\) cm.[[elif test="is(ans2=\"meet\")"]]The arcs do meet: the diagram shows them crossing above and below \(AB\). Look at the line that is drawn.[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]Your choice says the line is not at right angles to \(AB\). Each crossing point is {@exd(R1)@} cm from \(A\) and {@exd(R2)@} cm from \(B\), one above \(AB\) and one below, so the two are mirror images in \(AB\) and the line joining them is at right angles to it. Where does it cross \(AB\)?[[else]]Your choice says the line is at right angles to \(AB\). The line drawn runs from the crossing point above \(AB\) to \(B\): check that angle in the diagram.[[/if]]
